questions.question: It is the duty of every citizen to uphold and protect the _______, unity and integrity of India.
questions.questionHtml: It is the duty of every citizen to uphold and protect the _______, unity and integrity of India.
questions.solution: Article 51A of the Constitution states that citizens must protect India's sovereignty, unity, and integrity, respect its cultural history, show compassion for all living things, and pursue excellence. The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act added the duty of providing education to children aged 6-14. Upholding these duties is essential for national harmony and progress.

questions.question: The 11th Fundamental Duty provides opportunities for education for the ______ age group of children.
questions.questionHtml: The 11th Fundamental Duty provides opportunities for education for the ______ age group of children.
questions.solution: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, added Article 51A(k), mandating parents/guardians to ensure education for children aged 6-14 years. It also introduced Article 21A, establishing free, compulsory education as a fundamental right, promoting national and individual development.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties are contained within which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.questionHtml: Fundamental Duties are contained within which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: In the Constitution of India, fundamental duties are mentioned in Article 51A. Fundamental duties were added to the Indian constitution through the 42nd amendment, with 11 non-justiciable duties including respecting the national flag and promoting harmony. The idea was borrowed from the Russian constitution.

questions.question: The fundamental duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of 6 and ________.
questions.questionHtml: The fundamental duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of 6 and ________.
questions.solution: The Right to Education Act mandates parents to provide education to children aged 6-14. The act aims to provide free and compulsory education to all children in India, prohibits private tuition, reserves 25% of seats in private schools for economically weaker sections, and establishes primary and upper primary schools within a certain distance from a child's house.

questions.question: The total number of fundamental duties provided by the Constitution of India is:
questions.questionHtml: The total number of fundamental duties provided by the Constitution of India is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 11.

  • The total number of fundamental duties provided by the Constitution of India is 11.

Key Points

  • The 11 fundamental duties are:
  1. to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
  2. to cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom
  3. to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India
  4. to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so;
  5. to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women
  6.  to value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture
  7.  to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures
  8.  to develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform
  9.  to safeguard public property and to abjure violence
  10.  to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.
  11. to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years. This duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

Additional Information

  • The fundamental duties of the Indian constitution were borrowed from the USSR Constitution.
  • By the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, the fundamental duties of the Indian constitution were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976.
  • Article 51A deals with the fundamental duties of the Indian citizen.
  • The fundamental duties are non-justiciable.

Important Points

  • Father of Indian Constitution - Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
  • National Constitution day - 26th November.
  • The total number of parts in the Indian Constitution- 25.
  • The total articles in the Indian Constitution - 470.
  • The total number of schedules - 12.

questions.solution: The housemaid violates Article 51A(k) of the Indian Constitution, which mandates that every citizen must provide opportunities for their child's education. By making her 12-year-old daughter work instead of sending her to school, she neglects this duty. Education is crucial for the child's development and empowerment, and its denial also raises issues of child labor, prohibited under laws like the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986. Article 51A outlines various fundamental duties of citizens, including respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, safeguarding public property, and protecting the environment.

questions.question: Which Article states that it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to abide by the constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem?
questions.questionHtml: Which Article states that it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to abide by the constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem?
questions.solution: Article 51A (a) of the Indian Constitution, part of the Fundamental Duties introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, states that every citizen must abide by the Constitution, respect its ideals, institutions, National Flag, and National Anthem. These duties emphasize citizens' responsibilities and are inspired by the former USSR Constitution.

questions.question: In which year were the Fundamental Duties of citizens added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment?
questions.questionHtml: In which year were the Fundamental Duties of citizens added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1976.

  • In 1976 the Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment.

Key Points

  • 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 is one of the most important amendments to the Indian Constitution. It was enacted by the Indian National Congress headed by Indira Gandhi.
  • Due to the large number of amendments this act has brought to the Indian Constitution, it is also known as Mini-Constitution. The topic 42nd Amendment Act also called The Constitution Act, 1976.
  • 42nd Amendment Act amended/ introduced various provisions given below:
    • Attempted to reduce the power of the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
    • Laid down Fundamental Duties for citizens.

Additional Information

Changes in Provisions by the 42nd Amendment Act Details of the Amendment
Preamble
  • Words Socialist, Secular, and Integrity added. 
7th Schedule
  • Transferred five subjects from the state list to the concurrent list:
    • Education, Forests, Weights & Measures, Protection of Wild Animals and Birds, and Administration of Justice.
Article 51A
  • 10 Fundamental Duties added for the citizens. (The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee that was constituted by the government in 1976).

questions.solution: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution in Part IV-A by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, based on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendations. The committee proposed including a duty to pay taxes and penalties for violation of duties.

questions.question: How many fundamental duties of Indian citizens are there in the Indian Constitution, as of March 2022?
questions.questionHtml: How many fundamental duties of Indian citizens are there in the Indian Constitution, as of March 2022?
questions.solution: As of March 2022, there are 11 fundamental duties of Indian citizens in the Indian Constitution. These duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1976 and are listed under Article 51A. The duties include upholding the Constitution and respecting national symbols, protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India, promoting harmony and renouncing practices derogatory to women, valuing and preserving the country's heritage, and striving towards excellence. The 86th Amendment Act added the duty of providing education to children between the ages of six and fourteen.

questions.solution: The Fundamental Duties, incorporated in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, are specified in Part IVA (Article 51A). There are 11 duties that promote discipline, patriotism, and unity among citizens, such as respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property. These duties, modeled on the Soviet Constitution, are moral obligations rather than enforceable laws. The 42nd Amendment, known as the "Mini-Constitution," also introduced significant changes like adding "Socialist" and "Secular" to the Preamble and extending the legislative term. Mandatory national service of 5 years is not a Fundamental Duty.

questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?

options.text: To prohibit trade in rare and endangered species
options.html: To prohibit trade in rare and endangered species

options.html: To value and preserve rich heritage of the country's composite culture

options.html: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence

options.html: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is To prohibit trade in rare and endangered species.

Key Points

  • Fundamental Duties are a set of moral obligations enshrined in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution.
  • These duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
  • They aim to promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of India.
  • While the fundamental duties do not include "To prohibit trade in rare and endangered species," they do consist of duties like respecting the national flag, cherishing the heritage, and protecting the environment.

Additional Information

  • Fundamental Duties
    • Fundamental Duties are outlined in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
    • There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed for the citizens of India.
    • Some of the key duties include respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and developing a scientific temper.
    • These duties act as a reminder to citizens that while they enjoy their rights, they also have responsibilities towards the nation.
  • 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
    • Often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact on the Indian Constitution.
    • It was enacted during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.
    • In addition to introducing the Fundamental Duties, it also added the words "Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity" to the Preamble.
    • The amendment brought significant changes to the Constitution, including the extension of the duration of legislatures, administrative reforms, and judicial reforms.
  • Swaran Singh Committee
    • Formed in 1976 to make recommendations on constitutional amendments.
    • The committee was headed by Swaran Singh, a senior Congress leader and former Union Minister.
    • Its primary recommendations included the inclusion of Fundamental Duties and strengthening the Centre's power.
    • The committee's recommendations laid the groundwork for the 42nd Amendment Act.
  • Environment Protection
    • While the Fundamental Duties do not explicitly mention prohibiting trade in rare and endangered species, they do emphasize the protection and improvement of the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
    • Citizens are encouraged to develop a sense of environmental responsibility and contribute to the preservation of biodiversity.
    • Various laws and policies, such as the Wildlife Protection Act, are in place to regulate and prohibit such trade.
    • These efforts are crucial for maintaining ecological balance and safeguarding the country's natural heritage.

questions.question: The 42 nd amendment of the Indian Constitution added ________.
questions.questionHtml: The 42<sup>nd</sup> amendment of the Indian Constitution added ________.
questions.solution: The 42nd Amendment of the Indian Constitution, enacted in 1976, added Part IVA, introducing ten Fundamental Duties under Article 51A. These duties emphasize citizens' responsibilities alongside their rights, including respecting national symbols, upholding freedom struggle ideals, and protecting India's sovereignty and integrity. Known as the "Mini-Constitution," this amendment brought extensive changes, enhancing central government power and altering the Preamble, Seventh Schedule, and various articles. Enacted during the Emergency by Indira Gandhi's government, it remains controversial due to its significant impact on central-state power dynamics.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is To promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood.

Key Points

  • The fundamental duty to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, regional, or sectional diversities is crucial in maintaining unity in diversity.
  • This duty highlights the importance of respecting and tolerating different beliefs and practices within the country.
  • It encourages citizens to rise above narrow considerations of caste, creed, and religion and to work towards the welfare of society as a whole.
  • Promoting harmony and brotherhood is essential for fostering an environment where different communities can coexist peacefully and contribute to national development.

Additional Information

  • Fundamental Duties:
    • Fundamental Duties are a set of moral obligations that all citizens are expected to follow and respect.
    • These duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, under Article 51A.
    • Initially, there were ten fundamental duties, and later, an eleventh duty was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
    • Although these duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable, they serve as a constant reminder of the responsibilities that come with citizenship.
  • Promoting Harmony and Brotherhood:
    • This duty is essential in a multicultural and pluralistic society like India, where people from various backgrounds coexist.
    • It emphasizes the need for mutual respect, tolerance, and understanding among different communities.
    • By promoting harmony, citizens can help prevent conflicts and ensure a peaceful and cohesive society.
    • This duty also underscores the importance of national integration and unity, which are vital for the country's progress and development.
  • Respect for Diversity:
    • India is known for its rich cultural, religious, and linguistic diversity.
    • Respecting this diversity is crucial for maintaining social harmony and fostering a sense of belonging among all citizens.
    • Encouraging dialogue and interaction between different communities can help bridge gaps and build stronger relationships.
    • Diversity should be seen as a strength and a source of inspiration for collective growth and development.

questions.question: When were the Fundamental Duties first included in the Indian Constitution?
questions.questionHtml: When were the Fundamental Duties first included in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1976.

Key Points

  • Fundamental Duties:-
    • The Fundamental Duties were first included in the Indian Constitution in 1976. This was through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, which was enacted during the Emergency period.
    • The amendment added ten Fundamental Duties to Part IV-A of the Constitution. These duties were considered to be complementary to the Fundamental Rights, which had been included in the Constitution at its inception in 1950.
    • The Fundamental Duties are intended to remind citizens of their obligations to the nation and to each other. They are not legally enforceable, but they are considered to be important moral and ethical principles.
    • The 86th Constitutional Amendment, enacted in 2002, added another Fundamental Duty, bringing the total to eleven.

Additional Information

  • The eleven Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens:
    • Abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
    • Honour the motherland and its rich heritage, culture and traditions.
    • Promote harmony and national integration and the respect for different religions, languages and cultures.
    • Render selfless service to the country and to put nation above self.
    • Protect public property and abjure violence.
    • Strive to achieve excellence in all spheres individual activity.
    • Pay taxes honestly and contribute to public savings.
    • Protect and improve the natural environment and forests, lakes, mountains and rivers.
    • Have compassion for living creatures.
    • Uphold the dignity of women and children against exploitation and abuse.
    • Provide opportunities for education to his children, as it is the fundamental duty of each parent or guardian.

questions.question: With reference to Indian Constitution, Which of the following statements is correct regarding Fundamental duties?
questions.questionHtml: With reference to Indian Constitution, Which of the following statements is correct regarding Fundamental duties?

options.text: Non-justiciable in the court of law when it is violated
options.html: Non-justiciable in the court of law when it is violated

options.text: Not amended after their inclusion in 42nd amendment
options.html: Not amended after their inclusion in 42nd amendment

options.text: Punishable in the court of law when it is violated
options.html: Punishable in the court of law when it is violated

options.text: Not Enforceable through Law of Parliament
options.html: Not Enforceable through Law of Parliament

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Non-justiciable in the court of law when it is violated.

Key Points

  • Fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced through the court of law.
  • They were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.
  • These duties serve as moral obligations for citizens to promote a sense of discipline and commitment to the nation.
  • There is no direct penalty or punishment for violating Fundamental Duties unless specific laws are enacted by the Parliament to enforce them.
  • Currently, the Constitution lists 11 Fundamental Duties, which include respecting national symbols, protecting the environment, and upholding the spirit of the Constitution.

Additional Information

  • Fundamental Duties: Incorporated under Article 51A of the Constitution, these duties apply to every citizen of India.
  • 42nd Amendment Act: This amendment was enacted during the Emergency era in 1976, introducing Fundamental Duties as part of efforts to instill discipline among citizens.
  • Non-Justiciable Nature: Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-enforceable in courts. However, laws can be made to give effect to these duties.
  • Key Examples of Duties: Some of the duties include abiding by the Constitution, respecting national symbols, safeguarding public property, and promoting harmony.
  • Global Inspiration: The concept of Fundamental Duties draws inspiration from socialist constitutions like that of the USSR, aiming to balance citizen rights with responsibilities.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution says "the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities”?
questions.questionHtml: Which article of the Indian constitution says "the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 51A.

Key Points

  • Article 51A is part of the Fundamental Duties enshrined in the Indian Constitution under Part IVA, which was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
  • The Article states that it is the duty of every citizen to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, regional, and sectional diversities.
  • This duty also emphasizes renouncing practices that are derogatory to the dignity of women and fostering a sense of unity and integrity in the country.
  • Fundamental Duties under Article 51A are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law but act as moral obligations for citizens.
  • Article 51A consists of a total of 11 Fundamental Duties, including the duty to protect the environment, preserve the heritage, and uphold the Constitution.

Additional Information

  • Fundamental Duties:
    • Introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
    • Fundamental Duties serve as a reminder for citizens to uphold the spirit of patriotism and contribute to the nation’s welfare.
  • Part IVA of the Constitution:
    • This part was added to incorporate Fundamental Duties as a distinct section, inspired by the Constitution of the former USSR.
    • These duties emphasize the ethical responsibilities of citizens towards the state and society.
  • 42nd Amendment Act, 1976:
    • Known as the "Mini-Constitution," it brought significant changes, including the introduction of Fundamental Duties and changes to the Preamble.
    • It aimed to enhance the authority of the central government and promote national unity.
  • Non-Justiciability of Fundamental Duties:
    • Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties cannot be enforced in a court of law.
    • However, they act as guiding principles for citizens to uphold constitutional values and responsibilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is a violation of the 7th fundamental duty related to the environment and wildlife?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a violation of the 7th fundamental duty related to the environment and wildlife?

options.text: Work for the betterment of the wildlife
options.html: Work for the betterment of the wildlife

options.text: To prohibit exploitation of protected species
options.html: To prohibit exploitation of protected species

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1) Trafficking of wildlife animals.

Key Points

  • Trafficking of wildlife animals is a direct violation of the 7th fundamental duty in the Indian Constitution, which calls for the protection and improvement of the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
  • The fundamental duty under Article 51A(g) mandates citizens to have compassion for living creatures and safeguard wildlife.
  • Illegal wildlife trade leads to the exploitation and endangerment of protected species, negatively impacting biodiversity and ecosystems.
  • Efforts to combat wildlife trafficking are supported by various laws in India, such as the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, which aims to protect animal species and their habitats.

Additional Information

  • Wildlife Protection Act, 1972:
    • This Act provides for the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants with a view to ensure the ecological and environmental security of India.
    • It includes provisions for the establishment of protected areas, the regulation of hunting, and penalties for violations.
  • Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES):
    • India is a signatory to CITES, which aims to ensure that international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten their survival.
  • Biodiversity:
    • Biodiversity refers to the variety of life on Earth, including the variety of species, ecosystems, and genetic diversity within species.
    • Conservation of biodiversity is crucial for ecosystem stability, human survival, and the overall health of the planet.
  • Environmental Impact:
    • Illegal wildlife trade can lead to the extinction of species, disrupt ecosystems, and result in the loss of biodiversity.
    • It also has broader social and economic impacts, including the potential spread of diseases and loss of livelihoods for communities dependent on wildlife tourism.

Additional Information
Other Fundamental Duties include:

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution is related with, to assemble peacefully and without arms?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution is related with, to assemble peacefully and without arms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 19(1) (b)Key Points

  • Article 19(1)(b) of the Indian Constitution guarantees to all its citizens the right to assemble peacefully and without arms.
  • This fundamental right underscores the democratic principle that allows citizens to gather for peaceful purposes such as protests, meetings, and processions, provided they do not bear arms or incite violence.
  • The right to assemble is subject to reasonable restrictions in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, public order, and maintaining the decorum of public places.

Clarification of Other Options

  • Article 19(1)(a): Guarantees the freedom of speech and expression to the citizens of India.
  • Article 19(1)(d): Entitles every citizen to move freely throughout the territory of India.
  • Article 19(1)(c): Gives all citizens the right to form associations or unions.

Additional Information

  • The provisions of Article 19(1) emphasize the balance between individual liberties and the need for social control to maintain public order and national integrity.
  • These rights, while fundamental, are not absolute and can be restricted under specified conditions to ensure they are exercised without adversely affecting the society or the state.
  • The right to assemble peacefully is a cornerstone of democratic societies, facilitating dialogue and interaction between the government and its citizens, promoting transparency, accountability, and participatory governance.

questions.question: Who was the Prime Minster of India when the Fundamental Duties were first incorporated in the Constitution of India?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the Prime Minster of India when the Fundamental Duties were first incorporated in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indira Gandhi

Key Points

  • Indira Gandhi was the Prime Minister of India when the Fundamental Duties were first incorporated in the Constitution of India.
  • The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of the Constitution in 1976.
  • The amendment added a new part, Part IV-A, which consists of a single Article, Article 51A, that enumerates the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
  • The idea of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.
  • These duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have certain duties towards the nation.

Additional Information

  • The 42nd Amendment Act is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the large number of changes it brought to the Constitution.
  • The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law.
  • There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A, which include duties such as respecting the national symbols, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, and protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India.
  • These duties are meant to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens towards the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution enshrines that if we are observing any religious procession, then we need to remember communal harmony?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution enshrines that if we are observing any religious procession, then we need to remember communal harmony?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 51A (e).

Key Points

  • Article 51A(e) of Indian Constitution: To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
  • It enshrines the obligation to foster unity and a spirit of fraternity among all Indians, irrespective of their religious, linguistic, regional, or sectional differences.
  • This speaks directly to the obligation to take into account social peace even when taking part in religious processions.

Additional Information

  • Fundamental Duties:
    • Part IV A of the Indian Constitution contains Article 51A, which deals with the Fundamental Duties.
    • The Soviet Constitution (USSR) is where the idea of fundamental duties originated.
    • Fundamental Duties were recommended in 1976 by the Swaran Singh Committee.
    • Ten Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
    • Fundamental duties are not subject to legal action unless specifically stated in a provision, in contrast to fundamental rights, which are justiciable.
  • The 11 fundamental duties under Article 51A are:
    • (a) to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem;
    • (b) to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom;
    • (c) to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India;
    • (d) to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so;
    • (e) to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women;
    • (f) to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture;
    • (g) to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures;
    • (h) to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform;
    • (i) to safeguard public property and to abjure violence;
    • (j) to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement and
    • (k) who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

questions.question: Fundamental duties are ________ and not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
questions.questionHtml: Fundamental duties are ________ and not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is statutory.

Key Points

  • Fundamental duties come under Part IVA and Article 51A.
  • These duties are statutory and are not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
  • Fundamental Duties in the Constitution are inspired by USSR.
  • Japan is the only democratic country, other than India, to have Fundamental duties in its Constitution.
  • These duties were incorporated through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 in the Constitution on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. 
  • Only 8 Fundamental duties were based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendation while the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act added 10 Fundamental duties in the Constitution.
  • Later, the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 was passed that introduced one more fundamental duty in the Constitution. Now there are Eleven Fundamental duties in the Constitution.
  • Rights and duties are correlative and inseparable.

Additional Information

List of Fundamental Duties of India

  • It shall be the duty of every citizen of India —
  1. To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem;
  2. To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom;
  3. To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
  4. To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so;
  5. To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women;
  6. To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture;
  7. To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures;
  8. To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform;
  9. To safeguard public property and to abjure violence;
  10. To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement;
  11. Who is a parent or guardian, to provide opportunities for education to his child, or as the case may be, ward between the age of six to fourteen years.

questions.question: In 2002, the number of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India was raised to:
questions.questionHtml: In 2002, the number of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India was raised to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 11.

Key Points

  • Initially, the Constitution of India included 10 Fundamental Duties under Article 51A, introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
  • In 2002, the 86th Amendment Act added the 11th Fundamental Duty.
  • The 11th duty requires citizens to provide opportunities for education to children aged 6 to 14 years.
  • This addition aligns with the Right to Education Act and emphasizes the responsibility of citizens toward universal education.
  • Article 51A: Lists the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens, which serve as moral obligations to promote harmony and contribute to the nation.
  • Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts but serve as guiding principles for citizens.

Additional Information

Aspect Fundamental Rights Fundamental Duties
Constitutional Provision Articles 12 to 35 Article 51A
Nature Rights guaranteed to citizens for their protection and freedom. Obligations for citizens to promote harmony and nationalism.
Enforceability Enforceable by the courts of law if violated. Not enforceable by courts but morally binding.
Examples Right to Equality (Article 14), Right to Freedom (Article 19). Respect the National Flag, and Constitution, and promote unity.

questions.question: Which of the following was not included when the writing of the Constitution of India was completed on 26.11.1949?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following was not included when the writing of the Constitution of India was completed on 26.11.1949?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fundamental Duties.

Key Points

  • Fundamental Duties were not included when the writing of the Constitution of India was completed on 26.11.1949.
  • The Constitution of India was completed on November 26, 1949, yet it came into force on January 26, 1950.
  • The date memorialized the celebration of Independence Day from 1930 by hundreds of thousands of Indians, who would gather in public, hoist the national flag and recite the pledge of independence in multiple languages.

Important Points

  • Fundamental rights are enshrined in part III of the constitution from articles 12 to 35.
    • These rights are taken from the constitution of the USA.
    • These rights are provided to all the citizens of the country without any discrimination. These rights made part III of the Indian constitution the Magna-Carta of India.
  • President's Rule in State is mentioned under article 356.
    • President's Rule can be imposed on any state of India on the grounds of the failure of the constitutional machinery.
    • President's Rule is imposed after the following condition:
      • The governor carries on with the administration of the state on behalf of the President. He or she takes the help of the state's Chief Secretary and other advisors/administrators whom he or she can appoint.
      • The President has the power to declare that the state legislature's powers would be exercised by the Parliament.
      • The state legislative assembly would be either suspended or dissolved by the President.
      • When the Parliament is not in session, the President can promulgate ordinances for the state's administration.
  • The emergency provisions are contained in Part XVIII of the Constitution of India, from Article 352 to 360.
  • The Constitution of India talks about three types of emergencies:
    • National Emergency in Article 352.
    • President's Rule in State is mentioned under article 356.
    • Financial Emergency in Article 360 of the Indian Constitution.
  • Under Article 352 of the Constitution, the President can only proclaim an emergency when she/he has a confirmation of the crisis by the Prime Minister and their union Cabinet presented to the President in written form.
    • Under Article 74, the President can remit back the written dossier for Emergency proclamation to the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.

Additional Information

  • Part IVA of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties.
    • There are 11 Fundamental duties.
    • Article 51A: Fundamental duties
      • To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
      • To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
      • To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
      • To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
      • To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
      • To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
      • To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
      • To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
      • To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
      • To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
      • To provide opportunities for education by the parent the guardian, to his child, or a ward between the age of 6-14 years as the case may be.
